commit.message:
The version gate crashed instead of reporting, and had already let its author past

Fixes #48, which diagnosed it exactly: the step fetched the base commit with --depth=1 and
then asked for a three-dot diff, which needs a merge base a shallow fetch cannot provide. Under
bash -e the git diff killed the step before any version was compared, and the maintainer was
shown "no merge base" -- a message naming neither the plugin nor a version. It reproduced only
in CI, because a local clone has full history, which is precisely why it passed review: the
logic was tested, the environment was not.

Three things were wrong, not one.

1. THE HISTORY. The checks now run in their own job with fetch-depth: 0, so the base is always
   reachable and the comparison can actually happen.

2. NO COULD-NOT-DETERMINE STATE. Every other gate in this repo distinguishes "the thing I check
   is wrong" from "I could not run" -- that is what exit 2 is for -- and this step had no such
   state, so an environment problem was indistinguishable from a verdict. It now checks that the
   base commit is visible and that a merge base exists, and says so in those words. It still
   fails CLOSED, because the alternative is silently shipping an unbumped plugin, but it fails
   legibly. A blocked PR with an unrelated-looking error is how a check gets switched off.

3. THE JOB NAME LIED. Both plugin checks lived in the job called `fetch_paper.py` and have
   nothing to do with it, so the red check in the PR list was named after an unrelated tool.
   They are now in a job called `plugin`.

AND THE GATE HAD ALREADY FAILED ON ITS AUTHOR. It ran only on pull_request. murderboard_
freshness.sh was changed and merged straight to main under an unchanged 0.1.0, so the check
written to prevent exactly that never applied to the person who wrote it. It now runs on push to
main as well, where the base is the previous tip -- for a merge commit, everything the merge
brought in.

That hole had already produced the real defect it was built to prevent: published content
changed while the manifests still said 0.1.0, so `/plugin update` was a no-op and the freshness
gate compared 0.1.0 against 0.1.0 and reported "current" -- the false current the whole design
claims to make impossible. Both manifests are bumped to 0.2.0 here, which is the repair, not a
formality.

Not fixed here, and worth a decision: the new `plugin` job is not in main's required status
checks, so it reports without blocking until it is added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

       # Runs daily in a scheduled workflow against a 14-day window that GitHub then
       # discards. A break is unrecoverable rather than merely annoying, so it is
       # checked here on every PR instead of being discovered a fortnight later.
@@ -168,21 +158,97 @@ jobs:
           python -m compileall -q .github/traffic_alert.py
           python .github/traffic_archive.py --help > /dev/null
 
+      # docs/index.html is served to the public by GitHub Pages. Its three
+      # load-bearing properties all fail SILENTLY: drop the doctype and every
+      # browser renders it in quirks mode (the gates table changes typeface, and
+      # only in a browser); add a webfont and "renders the same air-gapped" --
+      # which the page claims at its own top -- quietly becomes false; lose
+      # docs/.nojekyll and Jekyll eats anything Liquid-shaped. None of that shows
+      # up in a diff, so it gets a gate rather than a habit. The test carries its
+      # own negative controls: eight mutations it must catch, checked every run.
+      - name: the published page is still publishable
+        run: python tests/published_page_test.py
+
+  # ITS OWN JOB, AND THE NAME MATTERS. These steps used to live in the job called
+  # `fetch_paper.py`, which has nothing to do with either of them: when the version gate
+  # failed, the check a maintainer saw go red in the PR list was named after an unrelated
+  # tool, and the first thing they had to work out was that the name was lying. A status
+  # check that misdirects the person reading it is most of the way to being switched off.
+  plugin:
+    name: plugin
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      # fetch-depth: 0, DELIBERATELY. The version gate below compares against the base
+      # commit, and a shallow checkout has no ancestry, so `git diff base...HEAD` cannot
+      # find the merge base it requires and dies with `no merge base` / exit 128 -- before
+      # comparing any versions at all. That was issue #48: it blocked a PR with an error
+      # naming neither the plugin nor a version. It reproduced only in CI, because a local
+      # clone has the full history, which is exactly why it survived review.
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.10'
+
+      # The plugin manifests are exercised ONLY on a stranger's machine, at install time,
+      # after a push to main -- nothing here loads them, because a contributor working in
+      # the checkout uses the files directly. Same invisible-locally shape as
+      # docs/index.html, so it gets the same treatment. Three of the failures it catches
+      # (the two manifests disagreeing on the version, a hook naming a script that moved,
+      # the freshness gate losing the --plugin flag its own hook passes it) produce a
+      # plugin that installs, reports success, and does nothing.
+      - name: the plugin is still installable
+        run: python tests/plugin_manifest_test.py
+
       # A FORGOTTEN VERSION BUMP IS A FALSE "CURRENT", which is the one verdict the
       # freshness gate promises never to produce. `claude plugin update` keys on the
-      # version string: ship changed files under an unchanged version and nobody's
-      # update does anything, while murderboard_freshness.sh --plugin compares the two
-      # equal numbers and reports current. Both failures are silent and both land on
-      # strangers, so the bump is checked here rather than remembered.
+      # version string: ship changed files under an unchanged version and nobody's update
+      # does anything, while murderboard_freshness.sh --plugin compares the two equal
+      # numbers and reports current. Both failures are silent and both land on strangers.
+      #
+      # IT RUNS ON PUSH TO MAIN AS WELL AS ON PRs. PR-only was itself a hole, and the
+      # author fell straight through it: murderboard_freshness.sh was changed and merged
+      # directly to main under an unchanged 0.1.0, so the gate built to prevent exactly
+      # that never applied to the person who wrote it. On a push the base is the previous
+      # tip, which for a merge commit covers everything the merge brought in.
       #
-      # Scoped to the files that actually change plugin BEHAVIOUR. A README fix or a
-      # traffic-bot commit ships in the tree too (source is "./") but changes nothing a
-      # user runs, and demanding a release for it would train people to bump blindly.
+      # Scoped to the files that change plugin BEHAVIOUR. A README fix or a traffic-bot
+      # commit ships in the tree too (source is "./") but changes nothing a user runs, and
+      # demanding a release for those would train people to bump blindly.
       - name: the plugin version was bumped if the plugin changed
-        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'push'
         run: |
-          base='${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}'
-          git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin "$base" 2>/dev/null || true
+          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
+            base='${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}'
+          else
+            base='${{ github.event.before }}'
+          fi
+
+          # A first push to a new branch reports an all-zero "before" and there is nothing
+          # to compare against.
+          case "$base" in
+            ''|0000000000000000000000000000000000000000)
+              echo "no base commit to compare against — nothing to check"; exit 0 ;;
+          esac
+
+          # REPORT, DO NOT CRASH. Without this the step dies inside `git diff` under
+          # `bash -e` and the maintainer is told "no merge base", which says nothing about
+          # plugin versions. The other gates in this repo all have a distinct
+          # could-not-determine state; this is that state, and it fails CLOSED, because
+          # the alternative is silently shipping an unbumped plugin.
+          if ! git cat-file -e "$base^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
+            echo "::error::cannot see base commit $base, so the version check could not run."
+            echo "::error::This is a CI history problem, not a plugin problem — the job needs"
+            echo "::error::fetch-depth: 0. Nothing is known about whether a bump was needed."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          if ! git merge-base "$base" HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            echo "::error::no merge base between $base and HEAD, so the version check could"
+            echo "::error::not run. This is a CI history problem, not a plugin problem."
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
           changed=$(git diff --name-only "$base"...HEAD -- \
                       skills hooks commands agents .claude-plugin \
                       doc_review_process.md fetch_paper.py \
